notes.problem: Close crop on the primitive kit steer. The hide texture is smeared, the back contour is doubled at about y 680 to 760, the ear flap cuts through the horn and the legs are bare cylinders. The model is biggest exactly where it is weakest.

The kit steer is smoothed and toy-like at full size, the tag is salmon rather than dusk gold, the rail crosses the body rather than the head coming through it, and the bunk lip and windrow the storyboard promised are missing from the bottom third.
The bunk sections fill only a thin band from y 1080 to 1340, about an eighth of the frame, between an empty sky above and an empty apron and labels below. The subject doesn't own the frame.
The four-section bunk fills about 15 percent of the frame height inside a large empty dark band, so the subject does not own the frame.

The page hangs before a flat mauve mid-tone backdrop with no true black. The quote's DOM type is axis-aligned while the sheet is skewed, so the words don't sit on the paper, and QA warns of a dead lower zone.
The page hangs against a flat plum mid-tone wall with no sky, no yard and no throat under it. It is the deck's one grey-middle frame and fails the stage test.
The steers are about 40 px tall, the lamp pools are dim brown smudges that stop short of their fences, and both labels sit on dark plates. Fence lines outweigh the lit pens at 432 px.
The labels sit on dark plates, and the cattle and near triplet are too small at 30 m to read as pens.
The far 17 steers dissolve into the dark, so the 5-of-22 isotype the dek promises can't be counted at feed size.
The bunk's outer wall is the largest object and the least modelled, a clean pale slab with hairline joints, and the steers' legs read cool lilac from the fill.
The cover is missing the storyboard's blank gold tag and the elevator on the seam, and the nearest steer's face is turned into the rail, so the hook's AI half has no image.
The kit figure stands in a stiff A-pose with plastic hair and flat shirt shading, and the pipe post rises directly out of her cap. It reads as a mannequin at full size.
The cream U slab with a navy interior reads as an abstract sculpture, not a precast feed bunk section on dunnage.
